title: Re-evaluation of carrageenan (E 407) and processed Eucheuma seaweed (E 407a) as food additives
authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS), Younes M, Aggett P, Aguilar F, Crebelli R, Filipič M, et al.
funder: European Food Safety Authority; requestor: European Commission.
result: Carrageenan, sulphated galactose and 3,6-anhydrogalactose polysaccharides, is not absorbed intact; 98 to 100% of high molecular weight carrageenan is excreted in faeces in several species. Poligeenan (weight-average 10 to 20 kDa) is not an authorised food additive. The existing group ADI of 75 mg/kg bw per day was made temporary, with the database to be improved within 5 years; brand-loyal 95th percentile exposure exceeded it by up to about 10-fold. Uncertainties included the low molecular weight fraction and the relevance for existing inflammatory bowel disease.
